statement: A BST is given as: a line with n, then a line of n level-order entries where -1 marks an absent child; each placed node consumes the next two entries as its children. All stored values are distinct. A final line holds k. Print the kth smallest and the kth largest stored values, separated by a space. Run an inorder walk with a live counter and stop the moment the counter reaches k - that visit is the kth smallest. The kth largest is the same idea mirrored: a reverse inorder (right, node, left) stopped at k. Avoid materialising the whole sorted array; the counter makes both walks stop early.
constraints: Values are positive; -1 marks an absent child.

example.why: Sorted order is 2 5 7 8 12 14; second from the front is 5, second from the back is 12.

hint: The counter lives outside the recursion (or is threaded through returns) - one shared count per walk.
mistake: Resetting the counter inside each recursive call; every subtree then reports its own first visit.
